text: Kulakundalinl:Kundalinl as sheis knowntoKaulas. Kundalinl:thesnake-likefeminine formof innerenergy which sleepsin ordinarypeople,arousedby Tantrik yogis. Lalita: a namefortheGreatGoddess;it hasovertonesof erotic joy. Layayoga:yoga which uses the principleof absorbinglowergrades ofenergyintohigher,up the successive levelsofthesubtlebody. lila:'play', eroticpleasure, joy, and cosmic activityfreefrom definite aim. lihgam:the penis,or a symbolofitas emblemofthe masculineDeity. Mahakala: 'Great time', the form of Siva in whichhis natureas Timeis revealed. Maharaga: the highest form of con- centrated passionate energy, aninner state in which the ultimate truthis experienced asa whole. Mahavidya: a female formin which one ofthe subdivided energiesof the Great Goddess appears andcan be worshipped. Mahesvara: 'the Great Lord', Sivaas Lordof Creation. mandala:a circular diagram used for concentrating cosmic and psychic energy. mani: jewel',a substitute term for 'vajra', which indicates the highest Tantrik Buddhist insight. Makara: a water monster, often shown vomiting out the waters of creation, fertility and time. mantra: a Sanskrit syllable or group of syllables, usedto concentrate cosmic and psychic energies. Maya: the Great Goddess as she who 'measures out' (Sanskrit v ma) space and time, both - in an important sense - delusory. Meru: the mythical mountain at the centreof the universe, from which flowallthe waters of creation. Merudanda: the spinal tubein the subtle body, identified with Meru. mudra: gesture concentrating a mean- ing and energy. Muladhara: the lowest cakra. Nada:sound,andthecosmicprinciple of vibration. Nadabindu:the Seedof the Universe conceived astheoriginal first vibration. nadl: channel in which energiesflow throughthesubtle body. Nirvana:theBuddha'sultimatestateof release,whenallKarma isexhausted. Nitya: a synonymfor Mahavidya implyinghereternalquality, nyasa: a riteoftouchingpartsofthe body to potentiatethemandidentify themwithpartsof theDeity. Om: the root mantraoftheworld, and themostpowerful ofall. Padma:lotus. paravritti: 'turning back up' theen- ergies ofthe subtlebody whichart- normally wasted. ParvatT: theGoddess as wifeof Siva. Patahjali: Sanskrit scholarand authorc. 150 BC. phur-bu: magician's dagger, aninstru- ment of power. Prakasa:the primalsparkof Creation. Prakriti: female agent inthe material creative process. Prana: inner energyofthesubtlebody. puja: practical worship-cum-ritual. pujari:one whodoes puja. Purana: Sanskrit collection of myth and legend. Purusa: male 'person' involved in the creative process. Radha:the chiefofthe GopTs. Riga: 'passion';alsoone ofthe emotive scalesof Indian music. Raginl:one ofthe 'female' scales of Indian music. Rajput: population group, mainly in northwestern India, whose tradi- tions were military. Rama: the heroof the Sanskrit epic Ramayana, adopted as an in- carnation of Visnu. Rasa: juice'; the 'tasting' ofa category of emotional experience. RasalTla-a term usedby followers of Krisna for blissful erotic play in celestial springtime. Red Hat:of the two principal divisions of Buddhist tradition in Tibet, that which is the more 'left-wing' Tantrik. Rig Veda: the oldest Veda, composedc. 1200BC. Sadasiva: 'Eternal Siva'. sadhaka: one who performs 1 ritual, worship and medil sadhana: the acts ofa sadhaka. SarasvatT:the Brahmin Goddessof DivineSpeechorChant, usually shown holding a musical instru- ment. sense-field (orsense-realm): a regionof experiencedefined byoneof the humansenses. Shaman:agifted ecstatic whoperforms trance dancesto makecontact with the supernaturalworld. Svayambhu: 'Self-OriginatedOne', a name appliedto Siva and hisem- blems. tanka:a Tibetaniconic painting, mountedsoasto provide a dwelling fora divineprinciple. Tantra:a textembodying Tantrik tradition,manyHinduexamples beingintheformofadialogue betweentheultimateDivine Couple, Siva and Sakti. Taoism:the Chinese 'Way'taughtin the ancient textsTaoTeChingand theworksofChuang Tzu.LaoTzu isitslegendaryteacher. Tara: aGoddessofWisdomin Buddhism; oneoftheMahavidya GoddessesinHinduTantra. Upanisads:Indianscriptures,ancient summariesofthenuclearphilosophy ofHinduism. usriisa: theprotuberanceonthe crown ofa Buddha'shead, signifying Enlightenment. Vaisnava: a follower ofVisnu. vajra:an emblemofpowerinTantrik Buddhism. Vajrasattva:one ofthe Supreme BuddhafiguresofTibetan Tantrik Buddhism. Vajrayana:TantrikBuddhism. Veda:themost ancientand sacred collectionsofhymns and legends preserved bytheBrahmins, in archaic forms ofSanskrit. Vedanta:the 'culmination' ofthe Veda, a name for theextreme monistphilosophy taughtespecially by Sankaracarya, c.ad800. Vimarsa: 'reasoning' or'discursive reflection',thefemalefunction 'mir- roring'theOriginal SparkofBeing. Vina:astringedmusical instrument. VTra:hero,well-developed sadhaka (q.v.) Visnu: one ottheprincipal High Gods otHinduism, in a variety ofin- carnationsincludingKrisna, Rama andtheBuddha. Void,the:theonlyadmissiblede- finitionfor theBuddhist experience ofultimatetruth. yoni:Sanskrit for the femalegenitals; theCosmicWomb.
